beats.did: 收到 Manhattan Remediation, LLC 从布鲁克林某地址寄来的一张“极其认真”的七十五美元账单；并顺手从店里拿走两副黑色 Wayfarers 太阳镜（为了好玩）。Claude 提议借她哥哥的车，从这家公司办公室跟到一次上门服务，再到 Silverman 说过的那个仓库。

anchors.anchor: I had gotten a bill for an extremely serious seventy-five dollars from Manhattan Remediation, LLC, from an address in Brooklyn.
I swiped two pairs of black Wayfarers from the store for fun.
Claude suggested that we borrow her brother’s car and tail them from their office to a house call and eventually to the warehouse Silverman had told me about.

beats.did: 十一点过一点 Claude 来接我；两人过威廉斯堡桥、沿 Greenpoint Avenue 北上，一路是仓库、车库、铁丝网（河对岸能看到 WNYC 的两座发射塔）；到了 Manhattan Remediation 的地址，那里没有招牌、楼上窗帘拉着，两人在车里听收音机等人。

anchors.anchor: Claude picked me up a little after eleven.
The address for Manhattan Remediation had no signage.
We waited in the car, listening to the radio

beats.who: Silverman 与另一名技术员 / 我们（跟踪）
beats.did: 正午看到 Silverman：他从店面出来，同行的男子穿着一样的 tech belt 和卡其裤、更老更胖、谢顶留马尾；他开了路边一辆车的后备箱查看、关上、坐进副驾。两人开一辆 Gran Fury（像警车，车漆上还留着条纹），我们一路跟到 Grand 街一栋铸铁楼（门前垃圾箱里是纸板、乱线、破木板）；一名穿灰色西装的女子拿剪贴板翻纸、指楼上，Silverman 点头进了侧巷；出来时女子递给他一只厚信封（现金？），随后他们又开走，我们跟到西侧肉加工厂的仓库（Royal Veal Corp. 和高架废轨旁），Silverman 与同伴从后备箱取东西进仓库，出来给门上锁、开车窜走。

anchors.anchor: At noon, we saw Silverman. He left the storefront with another guy wearing the same tech belt and khakis
Claude shook her head.
there they were, double-parked in front of a cast iron on Grand
We drove past them and parked in front of a hydrant a few car lengths up.
The woman with the clipboard handed him a thick envelope—cash?—and they were off again.
We drove one car behind them to the meatpacking plants on the West Side
Silverman and the other guy came out of the building, padlocked the door, and got back into the car and peeled off.

beats.did: 仓库挂着挂锁，两人还是敲了门，无人应答；我说起小时候的游戏——如果无家可归、要躲起来会去哪儿，并指出窗子、街那头的空垃圾箱和对街的牛奶箱、托盘，“We can build a way in.”；两人把锈垃圾箱推下人行道、把箱子搬过街，Claude 扶我上去，我爬窗而入；我向 Claude 要刀，她从靴子里掏出来递给我；我打开窗探头进去，然后跳进仓库、把梯子拖到窗边，让 Claude 攀进来。

anchors.anchor: Despite the padlock on the door to the warehouse, we knocked anyway. No answer.
We can build a way in.
After we pushed the rusted dumpster down the sidewalk and schlepped the crates across the street
She handed it over, predictably, from inside her boot.
I dropped down inside the warehouse
watching Claude pull herself up onto the window ledge

beats.did: 冷库门后不像是冰柜：从地板到天花板，无把手的金属抽屉像步入式卡片目录一样堆到至少十二英尺高，每格约四英寸高、十英寸宽，房间还往里延伸约八英尺；第一只抽屉上用美纹纸飞速写着“W10 11/8/83”“Charles 12/17/83”“1A 12/31/83”，抽屉按时间排列、地址多在下城、约三分之一未标记、日期越来越密（“word must be traveling”）；我读到自己的地址与当初打电话的那天“E7 7/8/84”，意识到那正是 Mark 死后一个月。

anchors.anchor: From floor to ceiling, metal drawers were stacked at least twelve feet like a walk-in card catalog
each about four inches high by ten wide
The first drawer was labeled, in fast handwriting on masking tape
about a third of the drawers were unmarked
I kept looking until I saw my own address and the date I’d called them
It was one month since Mark died.

beats.did: 我用瑞士军刀沿四角摸索找机关、未果（“There’s some give, but no mechanism to open it.”），最后用掌侧一拳，抽屉弹出来——不是抽屉，而是一只盒子，the cage：标签那面是金属板，其余是编织紧密的金属网，摇不出声、摸着越来越冷；此时 Silverman 站在冰柜门口喊“You can’t be here. You need to leave right now. You’re trespassing.”；我说“It’s not her fault… I broke us in.”，并说自己只想“get him out”，Silverman 让他把盒子放下。

anchors.anchor: It sprung right out—not a drawer, but a box, the cage.
You need to leave right now. You’re trespassing.
I broke us in.
I just want to…get him out.
You have to put it down.

beats.did: 我拇指沿盒子边缘摸索、指甲卡住网面想撬开（Silverman 举着对讲机喊 Walter 回来）；盒子突然滚烫，我把它掉在地上，它由银色变红，一声刺耳的摩擦声后——tzzt——冰柜的灯灭了；先是远处收音机般的多台人声，然后房间里那股“空”被一个巨大、滚烫的存在填满，我看到 François 伸出手臂、踉跄着扑向 Silverman，把他摁在墙上、又像与他重叠（François 的轮廓像被通电后描在 Silverman 身上），Silverman 眼里发狂、朝空中抓。

anchors.anchor: the box was burning hot. I dropped it to the ground, where it turned from silver to red.
the lights in the freezer went out
I saw François stretch out his arm and stagger toward Silverman.
pinning Silverman to the wall

beats.did: Claude 出声喊停 François，并讲起他问过的前一个房间里的老太太：她住在 Thompson Street 五楼、摔下楼梯断了髋骨、邻居叫了救护车却从未来探望、她是寡妇、儿子死在越南——她叫 Melina，她独自死去但已准备好离开；Claude 点头示意我“make my peace”。我低声念他的名字、道歉，先说不该送走他，随后坦白“I did want you to go”；他呜咽安静下来，转身离开、穿过我的身体，“And then it was over.”。Walter 赶到（问 Julian 是否还好），拾起空盒子检查、用遥控器逐格扫描，指出网面有一处“irregularity”、说该用更强的导体；Silverman 让 Walter 出去、随即让“我”出去，并说“You knew. You knew when you called us.”。

anchors.anchor: Claude called out
She lived on Thompson Street. Fifth floor.
Her name was Melina. She was in the room before you.
She was telling me to make my peace.
I did want you to go.
And then it was over.
You all right, Julian?
There’s an irregularity in the mesh here.
He stepped out of the way of the door.
You knew. You knew when you called us.

turning_point.text: 本章转折点：叙述者亲手撬开冰柜里封死的金属网盒（the cage）——François 因此现身并扼住 Silverman，叙述者第一次直面他的愤怒，在 Claude 的引导下坦白“我想要你走”，François 随即真正离开。

anchors.anchor: It sprung right out—not a drawer, but a box, the cage.
I saw François stretch out his arm and stagger toward Silverman.
I did want you to go.
And then it was over.

relations.pair: 我 ↔ Claude（伴侣/恋人，同案搭档）
relations.evidence: 叙述者越过身去吻 Claude，称她“real thoughtful”；她带了三明治、以护士的专业判断 Silverman 没有挫伤，并说“I’m a nurse.”。

anchors.anchor: I leaned over and kissed Claude.
I’m a nurse.

relations.pair: 我 ↔ Silverman（Julian）（前一客户 → 侵入者/看守者）
relations.evidence: Silverman 认出叙述者就是不久前打电话求助、对他的工作很感兴趣的那个人，脸色像被背叛；Walter 叫他 Julian。

anchors.anchor: He recognized me, the woman who had only recently called him for help
You all right, Julian?

relations.evidence: Walter 从对讲机应答“I’m double-parked, can you handle it?”，后被唤回冰柜；他提到“you and Rick”需要更强的导体，并说要把所有盒子扫一遍。

anchors.anchor: I’m double-parked, can you handle it?
I told you and Rick we needed to use a stronger conductor.

relations.pair: 我 ↔ François（死去的朋友，曾被我希望离开）
relations.evidence: 我承认“I did want you to go.”，此前也说过“I couldn’t handle it all on my own.”；他呜咽、转身、穿过我的身体后消失，把痛留在我身上。

anchors.anchor: I did want you to go.
I couldn’t handle it all on my own.
Before I shut my eyes to let him go
There wasn’t any sense of peace, or even release.

relations.pair: Claude ↔ François（安抚者；告诉他并非孤单）
relations.evidence: Claude 叫住他，讲老太太 Melina 如何独自死去、已准备好离开，最后说“Maybe she was looking out for you.”；叙述者点明她在说的是“他并不孤单”。

anchors.anchor: Maybe she was looking out for you.
It wasn’t unfinished business. It was loneliness. She was telling him he wasn’t alone.

relations.pair: Claude ↔ 她的哥哥（提及：哥哥的同性伴侣已死）
relations.evidence: Claude 说抽屉像 columbarium、是放骨灰格位的陵墓，她“older brother put his boyfriend in one of them.”；我问“You got a gay brother?”，她说“He’s not sick”。

anchors.anchor: My older brother put his boyfriend in one of them.
He’s not sick, if that’s what you mean.

relations.pair: 提及但不在场：Mark / Tanya / Melina / Bianca / Julie
relations.evidence: Mark：那天是 Mark 死后一个月，我想要“space for Mark”；Tanya：她说阁楼艺术家认证在收紧，她参与的团体想让市府把下东城破楼一美元卖出未果；Melina：Claude 讲述的前一位死者；Bianca 与 Julie：出现在童年/少年的外区记忆里（Coney Island、Jones Beach、高架废轨）。

anchors.anchor: It was one month since Mark died.
I wanted space for Mark
I heard from Tanya that they were cracking down on the certification you needed to live as an artist in those lofts
Coney Island with Bianca and our moms when we were kids
the abandoned elevated tracks where Julie and I used to sneak up in high school
